images.title: Thirds and fourths as twelfths
images.purpose: Show the method cue: when both denominators go into one number, here 12, both strips can be recut into that same fractional unit.
images.composition: Two upright paper strips standing side by side on one baseline with wide space between them, and one short cue line centred below.
images.exact_structure: Left: one upright paper strip cut across by thin lines into 12 equal pieces, with thicker lines after every 4 pieces marking thirds; the bottom 4 pieces filled teal #0072B2. Right: one upright strip of exactly the same size on the same baseline, cut into 12 equal pieces, with thicker lines after every 3 pieces marking fourths; the bottom 3 pieces filled amber #E69F00. Centred below: one cue line in reddish purple #CC79A7. Exactly 2 strips, 12 pieces each, 4 teal, 3 amber.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame

images.takeaway: Find a number both denominators go into, then rewrite both fractions in that unit.
images.description: Two same-size paper strips both cut into 12 equal pieces: the thick lines show thirds on one and fourths on the other, and the shading shows 1/3 = 4/12 and 1/4 = 3/12.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at one thick third and count the twelfths inside it, then do the same for one fourth.

image_decisions.why: Two strips recut into twelfths give the method cue without working any of the eight pairs.
